input: I was excited to try this location of Naked Tchopstix, but I was torn between giving it 3 or 4 stars. The vibe is different, more geared towards takeout, but they have a good-sized dining area too. Ordering at the counter was convenient, and I liked the customizable sushi bowl concept. However, the vegetable choices felt limited, and there was too much rice in proportion to other ingredients. The Maui roll didn't meet the same standard as the 96th street location. Despite these issues, I would still go back for the sushi bowls. The service may be slower, but it's worth it as a healthier alternative to fast food. And don't forget to try the yummy bubble tea, like the strawberry flavor!

input: We were hesitant to try the Shellfish Company due to past experiences with similar seafood places, but the positive Yelp reviews convinced us otherwise. The small restaurant requires planning and a wait, but our 20-minute wait during dinner rush was worth it. The $25 special of 3 lbs of California Rock Crab, salad, and choice of soup/chowder was a good deal. The rock crab was delicious and easy to crack, providing ample meat. The salad and chowder were satisfying, but the Shrimp Bisque was exceptional. Overall, a great value and one of our favorite meals on the trip. Ordering crab here is highly recommended.

If you find yourself dining at the Shellfish Company, we highly recommend indulging in their crab – you won't be disappointed.

input: I visited this location twice and had an extremely disappointing experience both times. The first visit was mediocre while the second visit was unbelievably bad. I ordered ribs and had to send them back because they were unevenly cooked, with one half warm and the other half refrigerator cold. Despite sending it back twice, the issue was not resolved until the third try. The manager apologized but didn't offer any compensation. I normally don't expect freebies, but receiving an insincere apology after three attempts to get my meal cooked properly really angered me. I won't be returning to this place.

input: I had a mostly enjoyable experience at Ava. The Ricotta cheese & toasted bread appetizer had great flavor, but the bread to cheese ratio was off. Both pizzas, sausage and potato with rosemary, were tasty, though they seemed to forget the Rosemary on ours. The grouper w/Israeli couscous entree was scrumptious. The zeppoles for dessert were amazing, but the cherry tart was not my personal favorite, although others at my table enjoyed it. I'll be returning to try their homemade pastas next time as they looked great.

However, the highlight of the meal was the grouper with Israeli couscous entree, which was absolutely scrumptious. Service is worse than if kindergarteners ran it. Embarrassing and a waste of space. Will never order from here again.

Regrettably, I have reached a decision that I will no longer be ordering from Silver Mine's.

The overall atmosphere is also negatively impacted due to the presence of typical casino gamblers, including inconsiderate smokers. In contrast, Cin Cin stands as a superior choice with its exceptional cocktails and a bar devoid of distracting machines. To enhance the overall experience, Peppermill should consider removing the machines, providing extensive staff training, and offering a more diverse range of independent liquors.

input: My sister-in-law and I visited this restaurant on 8/28/15 and it was a disappointing experience. Despite requesting multiple times, the hostess spoke too quietly for us to hear over the background music. We were seated in a booth with a never-ending Larry King vitamin commercial on the TV, which was not enjoyable. Our waitress introduced herself and a trainee, but they were absent for the rest of the meal and we were unsure who was responsible for our table. The food took a long time to arrive, considering the restaurant was not busy. The blue cheese burger had an overwhelming amount of blue cheese and could have been better with less. The fries and onion sticks were tasty though. No one came to check if we were satisfied or needed anything and it took two requests and waiting time to get a carry-out box. Additionally, another family had been waiting for their food since before we arrived, which was concerning. Overall, I do not plan on returning to this restaurant in the future.

Despite the tired decor and the unattractive strip mall location, the dishes such as Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani are perfectly seasoned, not greasy, and just the right level of spicy. Their attentiveness to special dietary requests, such as allergies, is commendable. Although it would be nice if they upgraded their surroundings, the food remains the highlight, making a return visit a must.

The full breakfast options like the crawfish omelet and Cajun hashbrowns were decent but, let's be honest, the beignets steal the show.

input:
I would strongly advise against choosing this place for any type of service or purchase. The lack of a dedicated customer service department is a major flaw. They rely on their sales team to handle customer inquiries, resulting in frustrating experiences where calls go unanswered or are directed to voicemail. Even leaving a voicemail for the manager proved futile, as they did not bother to return the call. 

During the car purchase process, I encountered several issues. Promised adjustments, such as removing tint on the rear window, were not fulfilled. Furthermore, the sales manager initially miscalculated the price, but I had to insist on sticking to the agreed-upon amount. These troubles persisted when attempts were made to remove the tint, necessitating multiple visits and a significant amount of time. 

Moreover, the service department proved equally unhelpful. When I sought guidance regarding a warranty claim for a leaky trunk, the lack of knowledge and assistance from the staff was disheartening. Given the poor overall service experience, I cannot trust them to properly address my concerns. 

In summary, having a dedicated customer service department is crucial for resolving complaints in a professional and timely manner. Relying solely on the sales team for customer service is not a viable approach. The salesperson tried their best, but the lack of support from management and other departments leaves a negative impression overall.

Overall, the service for our large group was adequate but not exceptional. One member received their food late, and the closeout process could use improvement. Adding a tip for the large group made the bill easy. 
I ordered the lamb kebab plate with rice and babaghanoush. The rice was well-cooked and aromatic, while the babaghanoush was delicious with extra olive oil. The presentation of the dish was pleasant. Unfortunately, the meat was dry and lacked sufficient marinade. This area needs improvement.
I've visited this restaurant before, and previous experiences were better, particularly during Ramadan when they offer an attractive and diverse buffet. The Ramadan buffet starts at 8:30, but it's best to arrive early due to high customer demand.

input: I recently tried out this Thai restaurant and I would give it 4-5 stars. It was my first visit and I found the food to be delicious. The shrimp spring rolls were especially fresh and the peanut sauce was tasty. The tom yum soup was a bit too spicy for my liking, but still had a good sour flavor. The pad thai and drunken noodle dishes were also enjoyable, although the noodles in the pad thai were a bit overdone. The portions were slightly smaller than other places in the area. The owner was friendly and attentive, even coming outside to talk with me about the food. The restaurant has a cute setup in a quaint house, but it may not be ideal if it's crowded. Overall, I think it's worth a try for Thai food fans. I used a Living Social deal, which made the total bill for two people, including an appetizer, soup, and a drink, to be around $24.

input: My husband and I reserved a Corolla-sized car online, but requested an upgrade to a Camry at Avis Rent A Car in Reno. After some discussion, we received the Camry we wanted. The staff was professional, but the rental price of $800 for five days seemed high. We had already purchased insurance for $150. The car itself was great during our vacation. However, upon dropping off the car, we found out that a weekly rate would have been just $15 more. The upgrade had cost us an extra $20 per day. I will not rent from Avis again, opting for Hertz or Dollar and making phone reservations instead. In hindsight, the extra insurance was unnecessary as my personal insurance covers everything.

input: Visited this eatery with a party of 8 on Friday, July 22. Great location for exploring the Quarter afterwards. Unfortunately, only 2 out of the 8 dishes ordered were tasty - the jambalaya and file gumbo. The rest, including red beans and rice, meatloaf, Mac and cheese, shrimp po boy, and chicken wings, were bland and a waste of money. The staff was nice, but overall the food was mediocre.

input: West Ave. Grill is a happy and charming spot in Jenkintown, popular among locals who enjoy dining outside with their dogs and children. The restaurant offers both a large and small indoor area, complete with a bar overlooking the parking lot and the nicer part of Jenkintown town square. The friendly wait staff and often present owner contribute to the welcoming atmosphere. Upon leaving, customers are offered complimentary Dum Dum lolly pops and newspapers to enjoy. The food at West Ave. Grill is consistently good, with highlights including fluffy and crispy pancakes and the delicious Kansas City breakfast. The only downside is that the big salads could benefit from a bit more variety and ingredients. However, the staff is attentive and always willing to make things right. Overall, it's a nice place worth trying out.

input: Sweet Confections on Magazine St had a beautifully sweet ending to our trip to NOLA. After a delicious lunch at Cochon, we stumbled upon this charming spot. We tried a chocolate cupcake with mocha filling and truffles in raspberry, creme brulee, and orange flavors. The cupcake was good, but the mocha filling stole the show. The raspberry truffle was my favorite, with its perfect balance of dark chocolate. The coffee was a delightful chaser, not too overpowering, and I didn't even need milk or sugar. The seating was nice, with enough room for our group of six. The service was great, with helpful staff suggesting flavors and labeling. I give it 4 out of 5 stars, as having one more staff member would benefit the overall service.

Additionally, clearer signage for ordering, picking up, and paying would be greatly appreciated.

It would greatly enhance the overall dining experience if they could provide clearer signage for ordering, picking up, and payment processes.

I heard about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite and decided to give it a try with my SO. We went on a Saturday morning and had to wait in line. 

The takoyaki appetizer was delicious - perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. The fried octopus was good but didn't come with enough mayo. 

Unfortunately, the ramen noodles were overcooked and didn't fit well with the dishes. The broth was flavorful, but the red chili one was too spicy and covered up the depth. I preferred the black garlic broth. 

Overall, the food was tasty and reasonably priced. The decor was nice, but there were screaming kids running around which made our meal unpleasant.

input: I recently enjoyed an express lunch at this charming restaurant with old school decor featuring dark woods and a copper tile ceiling. The deal included a choice of soup with the entree of the day, and I must say, the gumbo and crab bisque were fantastic. The gumbo had a rich flavor with a touch of heat from the andouille sausage, while the crab bisque was perfectly seasoned with old bay style seasoning and had just the right amount of shredded crab. The entree, garganelli with roast pork ragu, mushrooms, and creole tomatoes, was a delightful blend of flavors with a light sauce that highlighted the dish. The roast pork itself was tender, caramelized, and left me craving more. Overall, a satisfying lunch experience in a visually appealing setting.

input: I visited this place a year ago before the e.coli / colliform scare. Due to concerns for my health and safety, I haven't returned since. It's unfortunate because I genuinely enjoyed this place. However, I still have doubts about their ability to maintain proper food safety standards. My suggestion is for them to cook their meat thoroughly at 165°F to kill any bacteria, serve the food at a high temperature to ensure bacteria are eliminated, and only use greens and veggies sourced from the USA to avoid water pollution cross-contamination issues in Mexico.
0_Help me polish this:
I visited this place a year ago, prior to the e.coli/colliform scare. However, due to concerns regarding my health and safety, I have refrained from returning. It is truly unfortunate because I genuinely enjoyed my experience there. Nevertheless, lingering doubts persist regarding their ability to uphold adequate food safety measures. With that in mind, I would suggest a few measures to enhance their practices.

First and foremost, ensuring that meat is cooked thoroughly at a temperature of 165°F is crucial in order to effectively eliminate any bacterial contamination. Additionally, serving the food at a sufficiently high temperature would further bolster the elimination of bacteria and minimize any potential risks.

Furthermore, to mitigate water pollution cross-contamination concerns in Mexico, I would recommend sourcing greens and vegetables exclusively from within the USA. This precautionary step would help minimize the risk associated with contaminated water and bolster overall food safety standards.

By adopting these suggestions and prioritizing stringent food safety protocols, the establishment can reestablish trust among customers and assuage any uncertainties regarding their commitment to maintaining a safe dining environment.

input: Overall, this restaurant is small but conveniently located on the wharf. Despite the limited seating, the wait time was short. Sitting at the bar was a good option. The noise level was a bit high due to the small space. The service provided was excellent. The crab sandwich was disappointing, served on plain white bread. However, the fried shrimp was enjoyable - not greasy or heavy, with moist and flavorful shrimp. It is worth noting that the menu only offers shellfish options. As a non-seafood enthusiast, I was pleasantly surprised by the shrimp and onion rings. However, my seafood enthusiast husband did not enjoy the crab sandwich. If you love shellfish and appreciate the great location, this place could be worth a try.

input: I really wanted to like this place, but my experience was disappointing. The chicken was average, lacking flavor. The sauce options were limited for me, but the recommended mayo sauces weren't impressive. The mac&cheese was salty and mediocre, making a messy combination. The bananas foster pie had a great crust, but the filling lacked bananas and was mostly empty. The highlight was the birch beer, which was refreshing. The concept, decor, and menu are good, but the food quality doesn't match the price. 2 stars.
0_Help me polish this: I had high hopes for this place, but unfortunately, my experience left me disappointed. The chicken was just average and lacked any notable flavor. Additionally, I found the limited sauce options to be underwhelming, especially the mayo sauces that were recommended. The mac and cheese was overly salty and mediocre, creating a messy combination. Despite having a great crust, the bananas foster pie was lacking in actual bananas and left me feeling like it was mostly empty. On a positive note, the birch beer was a refreshing highlight. Overall, while the concept, decor, and menu seemed promising, the food quality does not justify the price. I would give it a 2-star rating.

input: Just visited The Fat Ham with my girlfriend and had a great experience. Small but nice vibe with welcoming staff. Impressive whiskey display. input: Finally tried this place after passing by so many times and I'm glad we did. Despite the small size, the interior is visually pleasing with wooden palates and two-tone gray walls. input: Brother Rabbit at Compere Lapin is a fantastic addition to the New Orleans food scene. From the refreshing house cider to the phenomenal Oban 18, the drinks are top-notch. The house biscuits and butter are simply divine, a must-try. While the crispy chicken skins lacked flavor, the rest of the first course menu, including the daily oysters and marinated shrimp with jalapeño jus, were delicious and fresh. Lastly, the dobeger cake with lemon curd and chocolate ice cream topped with a heavenly chocolate sauce is a perfect ending. Whether you're with a group or on a date night, Brother Rabbit is a great choice.

input: Impeccable food and service at Sbraga! The chefs counter 6 course with wine pairings was worth the price. The front row view of the deliciousness being prepared was amazing. The talented team ran like a well-oiled machine. Highlights include the Gruyere popover with foie gras soup, saffron spaghetti with blue crab, crispy Arctic char, and even the chicken liver mousse (surprisingly delicious). Seated in the front row, we had a mesmerizing view of the culinary masterpieces being prepared before our eyes. The level of skill and precision displayed by the talented team was awe-inspiring. 

The menu had a multitude of standout dishes, but a few truly stole the show. The Gruyere popover with foie gras soup was a mind-blowing combination of flavors and textures. The crispy Arctic char was cooked to perfection, with a tantalizingly crispy skin that contrasted beautifully with the tender flesh. The wine pairings were meticulously chosen, elevating the overall dining experience. Each sip perfectly complemented the flavors of the dishes, enhancing the dining experience to new heights.

To make the evening even more special, Sbraga surprised us with a personalized note and a thoughtful goodie bag to celebrate our birthday. It truly added a personal touch that we won't soon forget.

input: We decided to try this place after Terakawa had a long line, and we are glad we did. The service was excellent, and the staff was friendly. The waitress even helped my wife with her jacket while she was holding our baby. The Chicken Katsu Curry Ramen, Shrimp Katsu Ramen, and Shoyu Ramen were all delicious. The curry soup was flavorful, and the fried chicken and shrimp were cooked perfectly. We also enjoyed the pork buns, although they were not like traditional pork buns. Overall, we had a fantastic experience.

After being deterred by the long line at Terakawa, we decided to give this place a shot, and we're extremely pleased that we did. The service was truly exceptional, with friendly staff members who went above and beyond. It was heartwarming to see our waitress assist my wife with her jacket while she balanced our little one.

Now, onto the main event - the food. The Chicken Katsu Curry Ramen, Shrimp Katsu Ramen, and Shoyu Ramen were all outstanding. The curry-infused soup was bursting with flavor, while the fried chicken and shrimp were impeccably cooked, boasting a perfect balance of crispy outer coating and tender meat.

Though the pork buns might not have aligned with our expectations of classic pork buns, we found ourselves quite fond of them regardless. They presented a unique twist that still managed to captivate our taste buds.

Overall, our dining experience here was nothing short of phenomenal. We highly recommend giving this place a try.

input: I like Dewey's primary location for its proximity to my house. The pizza's appearance and crust are great. However, my main issue with Dewey's is its excessive saltiness. The pepperoni, Socrates Revenge, and Bronx Bomber pizzas felt like eating a brick of salt. The overwhelming combination of salty sauce and meat leaves my taste buds unable to detect any other flavor. If they address this issue, I would love Dewey's. The salads are decent in size but seem like something easily put together at home. I usually avoid ordering them due to the cost.

input: This is a typical Broad Ripple charming spot with a small, trendy, and bustling atmosphere. Unfortunately, they do not take reservations, which can be annoying for those traveling from another part of town. However, the cocktails were creative and delicious, and the server's suggestions were on point. The guacamole was tasty, but came with nuts despite requesting them to be left off. The Harvest salad was a highlight with its delightful combination of fruit and root vegetables. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both delicious, accompanied by interesting white sweet mashed potatoes. The Tostones were a bit dry, but dipped in the Stewed Black Beans, they tasted great. Unfortunately, there were no gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options available. Overall, it's worth a visit, just make sure to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to secure a table.

However, it's worth noting that reservations are not accepted, which can be somewhat inconvenient for those traveling from other parts of town. Nonetheless, the menu boasts a selection of creative and delicious cocktails, and the servers are adept at offering spot-on suggestions.

While the guacamole was indeed tasty, it was a minor disappointment that nuts were included despite specifically requesting their omission. On a positive note, the Harvest salad stood out with its delightful combination of fruit and root vegetables. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were nothing short of delicious, complemented by the addition of intriguing white sweet mashed potatoes. The Tostones were slightly dry, but when paired with the Stewed Black Beans, they became a delightful combination.

Regrettably, those with dietary restrictions may find the lack of gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options disappointing. Nevertheless, the overall dining experience is definitely worth a visit, as long as you make sure to arrive before 7 pm on a Friday to secure a table.

input: Momo's is a cool and upbeat place, great for groups or first dates. The tapas plates were delicious, especially the scallops. Portions were generous but ordering two at a time is recommended. The Greek salad's dressing was too sweet. The Spanish granacha wine was excellent and reasonably priced. The belly dancer was cute but the experience felt a bit awkward. Despite better Greek food options in town, Momo's is the go-to place for a fun night out. We'll definitely return.
0_Help me polish this:
Momo's is an exceptional and vibrant establishment, perfect for both large groups and intimate first dates. The variety of tapas plates offered were simply delectable, with the scallops being a standout choice. The portions at Momo's were impressively generous, although it is advised to order two at a time for optimal enjoyment. However, it is worth mentioning that the Greek salad's dressing leaned towards the sweeter side, which may not be to everyone's taste.

One aspect that truly stood out was the exceptional Spanish granacha wine selection, with its outstanding quality and reasonable prices. It provided the perfect complement to the tantalizing flavors of the tapas dishes. While the entertainment provided by the belly dancer was undeniably charming, the overall experience did feel slightly awkward, but this did not hamper the enjoyment of the evening.

Although there may be other Greek food options available in town, Momo's truly shines as the go-to place for a delightful and memorable night out. With its lively atmosphere and delectable cuisine, we will undoubtedly be returning to Momo's in the future.

input: I had high hopes for this place, but I was ultimately disappointed. The Dan Dan noodles were flavorful but lacked protein. The scallion pancakes were mediocre compared to another place I recently tried. The Wontons in Chilli oil were extremely spicy and lacked substance. The Talapia Medallions were fried well, but the greens were difficult to chew. The service and atmosphere were good, but I won't be going out of my way to eat here again. It feels too commercialized and Americanized for my taste. I prefer authentic Cantonese-style and hole-in-the-wall places.
0_Help me polish this:
I had initially held high expectations for this establishment, but unfortunately, my experience left me rather disappointed. While the Dan Dan noodles had a pleasing flavor, I found them lacking in protein. Moreover, the scallion pancakes paled in comparison to those I recently sampled elsewhere. The Wontons in Chilli oil, on the other hand, were excessively spicy and lacked substance.

Although the Talapia Medallions were fried skillfully, I found the accompanying greens to be quite challenging to chew. On a positive note, I must commend the service and ambiance, as both aspects were satisfactory. However, I don't anticipate making a special trip to dine here again. Personally, I found the place to be overly commercialized and too Americanized for my taste. I prefer the authenticity of Cantonese-style cuisine and the charm of hole-in-the-wall establishments.

input: We tried this place for the first time last night and overall, it was a good experience. The service was a bit slow, possibly due to the busy Saturday night during March Madness. The complimentary homemade chips were fantastic, although they took longer to arrive than my husband's salad. The restaurant had a kid's movie playing on one of the nearby televisions, which kept my 3-year-old entertained. The food was great, with my burger and seasoned fries being wonderful. However, my husband's blackened chicken was a bit too spicy due to being over-seasoned. My daughter's macaroni and cheese looked delicious, but she couldn't resist eating the chips instead. The seating arrangement inside was a bit odd, with a table located close to the women's restroom door. Personally, I found it strange and ended up waiting until I got home to use the restroom. On a positive note, they offer a 15% military discount, which was much appreciated. Despite the slower service, I would still recommend this place, although I would have given it 5 stars if the service had been a bit better.

input: This all you can eat place offers decent value at $27/adult, but the quality falls short when ordering from the regular menu. The maki rolls are average, but mine were too cold, indicating they had been pre-made and refrigerated. The oyster ponzu lacked the ponzu flavor and had a heavy coating comparable to an A+W onion ring. If you're extremely hungry and craving rolls and greasy tempura, this place is suitable. However, I recommend avoiding the squid.
0_Help me polish this: This all-you-can-eat place provides a satisfactory value at $27 per adult, but the overall quality of the food disappoints when ordering from their regular menu. The maki rolls are moderately tasty, although I found mine excessively cold, hinting that they had been prepared in advance and refrigerated. Additionally, the oyster ponzu dish lacked the desired ponzu flavor and had an unusually thick coating akin to an A&W onion ring. input: I was excited to try Lee How Fook after reading positive Yelp reviews, but unfortunately, I was left disappointed. The small size of the restaurant didn't bother me, but it's advisable to make reservations due to limited tables. The service was adequate, although understanding the server was a bit difficult. As for the food, the appetizers were delicious with a flavorful dipping sauce. However, the sweet & sour chicken was overly sweet and the vegetables were undercooked. The pan-fried noodle dishes lacked flavor and the supposed spicy beef wasn't spicy at all. Overall, I left full but unsatisfied.

input: I've been a member at this convenient and reasonably priced gym for a few weeks now and I'm enjoying it. input: My girlfriends and I dined at the Creole House for dinner due to its proximity to our hotel. The bacon garlic oysters were average, as the flavors were overpowered by the cheese and bacon. The jumbo buffalo wings were tasty and well-seasoned. The jumbalaya pasta lacked flavor and was our least favorite, while the blackened red fish was just okay. The sautéed veggies accompanying the dish were excessively salty. The canal street red fish wasn't great and lacked garlic sauce. The paddle boat drinks tasted good but were more juice than alcohol. Overall, the food was underwhelming, earning the restaurant a solid 3 stars. On a positive note, our server, Alexander, provided excellent hospitality and tried his best to ensure our satisfaction.

input: Prohibition is a nice, old school space with a long bar that feels reminiscent of western establishments, which is a bit unusual for Philadelphia. It's worth noting that Prohibition is located in a somewhat questionable neighborhood, which may deter some visitors from walking back if it's late at night.

input: Cake Life Bake Shop in Fishtown is a great find! The shop perfectly blends with the neighborhood vibe, and the clean and inviting interior is a plus. The assortment of stunning cakes assures top-notch bakers on board. I indulged in a variety of treats such as Bourbon Pecan and Chocolate Chip cookies, along with vanilla cupcakes with buttercream and raspberry icing. The Bourbon Pecan cookie stood out with its mild sweetness and delightful pecan bites, best paired with a hot coffee. Although the cupcakes were tasty in terms of cake, I wasn't entirely fond of the icing. Sadly, I didn't try the Chocolate Chip cookie, though everyone raved about it. Despite this, I'll definitely return and have Cake Life create a custom order; they have piqued my interest.

input: Western Cycle is a fantastic store for all your biking needs. From affordable kids' bikes to high-end racing bikes, they have a wide range of options. Their dedication to providing excellent service and maintaining an atmosphere of trust has solidified my continued patronage. While there may be other bike shops available, I only consider United Cycle as a potential alternative to Western Cycle due to their consistent quality and reputation within the industry.

input: Muriel's offers a delightful dining experience with its stunning views, haunted history, and delicious food. Make sure to explore the 2nd level for a tour of the lounge area and enjoy a fantastic view of Jackson Square from the wrap-around balcony. The indoor patio dining area is my personal favorite for its tranquil setting. The dinner pre-fix menu is a great value, with the seafood gumbo and dijon mustard encrusted salmon being standout dishes. The wood grilled pork chop for lunch was flavorful and tender, although the accompanying red beans and rice were a bit bland. Overall, Muriel's is a must-visit for its ambiance and quality cuisine.
